page: Microsoft Azure L80s_v3 is a storage-optimized virtual machine from the LSv3 family, hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor providing 80 dedicated vCPUs alongside 640.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include dedicated graphics accelerators, focusing entirely on high-throughput compute, memory capacity, and large-scale disk input/output operations.

A central architectural differentiator of the L80s_v3 is its integrated high-capacity local storage subsystem. The instance bundles 20,059 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Azure Premium Storage. The massive pool of directly attached solid-state storage minimizes latency and circumvents network storage bottlenecks, offering high throughput for transactional and I/O-intensive workloads.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the L80s_v3 delivers high density by combining large volumes of direct-attached NVMe storage with expansive RAM and 80 dedicated physical compute threads. The configuration balances substantial memory and core counts against extreme local disk capacity, making it a cost-efficient deployment for operations requiring multi-terabyte working data sets on host disks without recurring network storage transmission overhead.

The hardware profile makes the instance well suited for large relational databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, real-time analytics, data warehousing, and big data processing clusters such as Apache Spark and Elasticsearch where direct NVMe access and extensive RAM are critical.
description: Microsoft Azure L80s_v3 is a high-capacity, storage-optimized instance within the LSv3 series running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is built on an x86_64 Intel processor architecture, featuring 80 dedicated vCPUs, 640.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per vCPU), and no discrete GPUs. The virtual machine includes 20,059 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides compatibility with Azure Premium Storage. This design provides high I/O throughput and low-latency disk access for data-intensive processing without external storage bottlenecks. Given the dense combination of 80 dedicated compute cores, extensive system memory, and direct-attached multi-terabyte NVMe arrays, the L80s_v3 is structured for enterprise workloads including large-scale distributed databases, NoSQL platforms, in-memory data processing, search index nodes, and transactional data warehousing systems.
